notes: Identity checked in supplied text: title page identifies Milan Bischoff, University of Twente, 2024, with the exact replication-thesis title in ref_r. SOURCE URL https://essay.utwente.nl/100571/1/Bischoff_MA_BMS.pdf is consistent with supplied purl essay identifier 100571. This is a primary master thesis containing Methods, Results, Discussion, references, and analysis-code appendix, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No network verification performed. No PDF supplied; locations use canonical form-feed-separated text pages, counting title page as page 1. The source separates the direct male-only replication (Table 5, canonical page 19) from the extended mixed-sex analysis (Table 6, page 21). Each table includes cortisol AUCg and AUCi, five RFA definitions, and two electrode pairs. Candidate Table 5 pairs include average-pre F4-F3/AUCg r=.117, p=.523; average-pre F4-F3/AUCi r=.074, p=.686; same-day pre F4-F3/AUCg r=.265, p=.142; same-day pre F8-F7/AUCi r=.37, p=.037; post F8-F7/AUCi r=.401, p=.022. Candidate Table 6 pairs include average-pre F4-F3/AUCg r=−.045, p=.715 and average-pre F4-F3/AUCi r=.006, p=.960. All are printed Pearson correlations with exact p-values; none is assigned. Description does not specify cortisol definition, electrode pair, phase, or sex sample. No assignment uses row order, numeric matching, or original-page number. Table 3 explicitly gives final male-only N=32 and mixed-sex N=68. They are overlapping samples and cannot be summed. These are candidate final sample sizes, not established analytic N for an unspecified test. Methods reports 83 tested, sixteen excluded, and final 68, an internal accounting discrepancy; Appendix B instead lists 15 excluded identifiers. No recruitment subtraction or df-based N was used. Unassigned original and reported_success fields are placeholders. This row has no replication locator or requested replication metric. Results 3.1.2 additionally reports an RFA time main effect F [4, 124] = 6.92, p < .001, while experimental condition and its interaction with time are nonsignificant without numerical tests in that paragraph. The time effect is not substituted for a stress effect or cortisol correlation.
